branches.reason: First sample2 retained approach before actual rope; ordinary reload of that original save allowed a shorter pulse and sample4 of actual bidirectional rope. This is not a single monotonic-tick sequence or an automated replay.

observations.finding: Ordinary marker UI disallowed males. Save1 retains AllowMaleGender in disallowedSpecialFilters, while Deer remains in allowedDefs. Re-enabling males removed that filter before the ordinary roping order.

Ordinary context menu offered Prioritize roping Buck1. Save2 has playerForced RopeToPen/TakeToPen targeting Deer149579 and PenMarker149578, but rope state is still empty: it is approach, not attachment.

After ordinary reload of save2, save4 at76756 has deer.ropedTo=Thing_Human958 and handler.ropees=[Thing_Deer149579]; deer Wait has expiryInterval30 and queued FollowRoper. Inspector says Roped by: Prophet.

The first run save3 has deer at(125,0,141), inside the fence beyond the gate(124,0,141); ropes are cleared and handler resumed FeedPatient. Marker is green/enclosed, with nutrition consumption0.32. The later shorter-pulse branch also enters the pen before the gate experiment.

Ordinary Hold open toggle and drafted human movement through the gate yield Unenclosed(open door). Final identical selected-state saves at77990 retain open=True/holdOpen=True; deer remains player-owned and spawned. No roaming or exit was observed.
Animals roster shows allowed-area controls for Hare1, while Buck1 shows not in a pen. No area reassignment or return travel was tested.

shutdown.method: Ordinary Quit to OS at(2215,1315), after final duplicate save
shutdown.capture_result: Exit click was sent; post-exit foreground guard failed. No successful action100 record or exit screenshot exists.

limitations: Baseline75812 and preparation75813 show one tick of advancement despite pauseOnLoad preparation.

All buildings and tame deer were developer-prepared; no normal build costs/time or natural tame success are measured. The developer tame notification names Grump; it is not evidence that Grump performed ordinary taming.
First approach screenshot includes a job target line; save2 explicitly has no rope. Actual rope is established only by save4 and the inspector.
A normal reload creates a documented branch; save3 and save4 cannot be treated as chronological tick order.
Wall-clock pulses include scheduling/walking and are not job-duration calibration. The save ticks are authoritative.
No normal fence destruction, permanent escape, natural Roaming, species-filter exclusion, allowed-area travel, grass sustainability, birth or statistical probabilities were tested.
All samples are below300000ticks, so the five-day natural Roaming grace period has not elapsed.
Only selected XML projections/crops/hashes are public; full native screenshots and saves remain local.
